selection: User apply the suggestion after explaining ordered and unordered recovery on 2026-09-09. Applies only to this explicit candidate lane; legacy behavior is unchanged.
binding: Select one registered checked Workflow binding by exact workflow_sha256 and this definition hash. No raw graph, cloned checked object, or unversioned policy fallback is accepted.
dependency_semantics: needed-compensations-only: depends_on orders two compensation occurrences only when both forward steps are confirmed committed. Empty dependencies mean no semantic ordering constraint. Inactive dependencies are omitted from the selected plan but retained in authored source and explicitly recorded as inactive.
selection_and_order: Select only compensations whose exact for_step occurs in the confirmed completed prefix. Use the induced graph on that set. Topologically order active dependencies; among ready occurrences use reverse forward-completion order, independently of compensation declaration order. This deterministic tie-break is not a mandatory business prerequisite or permission for parallel dispatch.
journal: An owned closed failure journal names workflow_execution_id, failure_occurrence_id, the ordered completed_step_ids, the immediately following failed_step_id, and failed_commit_status. Only not-committed and indeterminate are permitted. Completed IDs must exactly equal the source prefix; failure must be the next declared step. This bounded journal covers failure of a forward Operation, not post-Workflow failures, parallel execution or durable storage.
unknown: An indeterminate failed commit produces reconciliation-required with no workflow_evaluation_result or Recovery Intent. Never treat uncertainty as non-commit, omit it as an unnecessary action, fabricate its result, automatically retry, or freeze a partial recovery plan around it.
outcomes: A known non-commit with no selected compensations yields evaluated/not-required with null intent. Otherwise it yields evaluated/recovery-required with one immutable candidate intent and ordered plan. These outcomes are not satisfied/unresolved terminal recovery dispositions.
identity: Intent identity binds policy, exact Workflow, execution, failure occurrence, failed step, completed-step journal and ordered plan digests. Each plan occurrence retains compensation ID, for_step, qualified Operation, checked action hash, active and inactive dependencies, and typed argument/Event binding expressions. Invocation identity additionally binds that exact occurrence and action. Pure deterministic planning does not enforce cross-call uniqueness, register intent, verify a provider, or provide replay protection.
business_conditions: Mandatory business conditions remain in declared Rule and Operation guards. The planner neither evaluates nor bypasses them and never executes compensation, rolls back committed facts, performs a lookup or writes data.
ownership: Closed bounded inert data is validated before field access, copied and frozen. Journal facts are caller-supplied; shape and source correspondence are checked, not actual commit truth. There is no arbitrary Proxy isolation claim.
compatibility: The existing occurrence source, checked Workflow binding, canonical D36/D37 documents, legacy recovery reference and old generated artifacts retain their bytes. No new meta-type or canonical relationship is added.
